newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea indicts President Kim Young-sam's son.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea indicts President Kim Young-sam's son.

text.p: The second son of South Korean President Kim Young-sam has been indicted on tax evasion and bribery charges, state prosecutors said on Thursday.

Prosecutors said Kim Hyun-chul had received from businessmen 6.61 billion won ($7.42 million), of which 3.22 billion was a bribe accepted in exchange for favours. Kim also evaded 1.48 billion won in taxes, they said.
Under Korean law, Kim could be jailed for life for tax evasion. The maximum jail sentence for bribery is five years.
South Korea's "crown prince," as he is derisively known, was charged with taking kickbacks from two alumni of his old high school, one a former top executive of a construction company.

Kim's May 17 arrest brought to a head a loans-for-kickback scandal involving top politicians, bankers and businessmen that emerged from the rubble of the January collapse of Hanbo Steel Co, the country's biggest bankruptcy.
The indictment of Kim, who remains in detention, came as authorities vowed to crack down on militant student leaders behind the worst street violence in Seoul in almost a year.
A six-day campus rebellion launched last week by the pro-Pyongyang Hanchongryon student group has been blamed for two deaths and hundreds of casualties.
Prime Minister Koh Kun vowed on Thursday to put an end to the violence and ordered the arrest of Hanchongryon leaders.
Hanchongryon on Wednesday took responsibility for the death of a suspected police informant who leaders said was beaten during an interrogation.
The students are demanding President Kim's resignation and details of his 1992 campaign spending.
Opposition parties insist his campaign spent at least 10 times the legal limit, and was partly bankrolled by the scandal-ridden Hanbo Group.
The founder of the Hanbo Group was sent to jail for 15 years on Monday along with bank presidents he had bribed and top aides.
